slides.caption: The depth every **3 hours**: 6, 4, 2, 4, 6, 4, 2, 4, 6 m. The tide **goes out**, then it **comes in**.

slides.title: How Many a Day?
slides.text: How many times a day is Mr Bowen’s harbour at **high tide**?
slides.textFr: Combien de fois par jour le port de M. Bowen est-il à **marée haute** ?

check.q: Mr Bowen’s harbour: how many times a day is the water at **high tide**?
check.exp: Twice: at 6 a.m. and at 6 p.m. Low tide is twice too: at 12 noon and at midnight. High to low takes **6 hours**. High to high takes **12 hours**.

slides.contentFr: Le port de M. Bowen : 6 m − 2 m = **4 m**.

notes.text: **Tidal range:** the difference in depth between high tide and low tide.
notes.textFr: **Marnage (tidal range) :** la différence de profondeur entre la marée haute et la marée basse.

notes.text: The Bay of Fundy: **16.3 m**. The Mediterranean Sea: **less than 1 m**.
notes.textFr: La baie de Fundy : **16.3 m**. La mer Méditerranée : **moins de 1 m**.

options.text: The difference in depth between high tide and low tide
The depth of the water at high tide
The time from high tide to low tide

check.exp: The tidal range is a **difference**: high tide depth − low tide depth. At Mr Bowen’s harbour: 6 m − 2 m = 4 m. It is not the depth at high tide (6 m), and it is not a time.

slides.title: The Deepest Water
slides.text: Average depth: **5.0 m**. Tidal range: **2.0 m**. What is the **maximum** depth?
slides.textFr: Profondeur moyenne : **5.0 m**. Marnage : **2.0 m**. Quelle est la profondeur **maximale** ?

check.q: The average depth of the water is **5.0 m**. The tidal range is **2.0 m**. What is the **maximum** depth?
check.exp: The range is shared: the water goes **1.0 m above** the average and 1.0 m below. Maximum: 5.0 + 1.0 = 6.0 m. 7.0 m adds the whole range to the average.

slides.title: Mr Bowen’s Boat
slides.caption: Read the four pictures. Where does the sea go? And why does it come back? The next slides tell you.

check.q: At 6 a.m. it is high tide. Mr Bowen ties his boat to the wall with a short rope. Why is the boat hanging from the wall at 12 noon?

options.text: It is low tide: the water is much lower
It is high tide: the water pushed the boat up

check.exp: From high tide to low tide takes about **6 hours**. 6 a.m. + 6 hours = 12 noon: low tide. The water went down, but the short rope did not. Sailors tie up with a **long** rope.

notes.textFr: **Force de marée (tidal force) :** l’attraction de la gravité de la Lune sur les océans.

slides.title: How Many High Tides?
slides.textFr: La Lune tire les océans. Combien de **marées hautes** la Terre a-t-elle **en même temps** ?

check.q: The Moon pulls the oceans. How many **high tides** does the Earth have **at the same time**?

options.text: One: only on the side facing the Moon

check.exp: **Two:** one on the side facing the Moon and one on the **far side**. The Moon pulls the near side most. The far side is left behind. So the Earth is stretched, and the water bulges on both sides.

slides.text: The Sun has the **strongest gravity** in the Solar System.

check.q: The Sun has the **strongest gravity** in the Solar System. Which makes **bigger** tides: the Sun or the Moon?
check.exp: **The Moon.** The Sun **pulls** the Earth harder, but it is 390 times further away, so it **stretches** the Earth less. Tides come from the stretch.

notes.text: The **Moon’s tidal force** pulls the oceans into **2 bulges**. The Earth **spins** through them: **2 high tides** a day. Tides are **biggest** when the Sun, the Moon and the Earth are in a **line**: at **full moon** and **new moon**.
notes.textFr: La **force de marée de la Lune** tire les océans en **2 bosses**. La Terre **tourne** à travers elles : **2 marées hautes** par jour. Les marées sont les **plus grandes** quand le Soleil, la Lune et la Terre sont **alignés** : à la **pleine lune** et à la **nouvelle lune**.

reveal.label: Who worked it out?
reveal.answer: In **330 BCE**, a Greek sailor from **Marseille** saw that the tides follow the Moon. In **1687**, Newton explained why: **gravity**.
reveal.answerFr: En **330 av. J.-C.**, un marin grec de **Marseille** a vu que les marées suivent la Lune. En **1687**, Newton a expliqué pourquoi : la **gravité**.

check.q: High tide is at **7 a.m.** When is the **next** high tide?
check.exp: High to high takes about **12 hours**: 7 a.m. + 12 hours = 7 p.m. 1 p.m. is 6 hours later: that is low tide.

steps.hint: High tide is the deepest water. Find the biggest number.

steps.title: Find the depth at low tide
steps.hint: Low tide is the shallowest water. Find the smallest number.

steps.title: Subtract to find the range
steps.hint: Tidal range = high tide depth − low tide depth.
steps.why: The tidal range is the difference between high tide and low tide.

slips.msg: 7 m adds the depths. The range is a difference: subtract.

steps.title: When is the first high tide?
steps.hint: High tide is the deepest water: 5.0 m.

slips.msg: 9 a.m. has the smallest depth, 2.0 m. That is low tide.

steps.title: When is the next high tide?
steps.hint: Find 5.0 m again, lower in the table.

slips.msg: 9 a.m. is low tide (2.0 m). Find the next 5.0 m.

steps.title: Count the hours between them
steps.line: High tide to high tide: @ hours.
steps.hint: Count on from 3 a.m.: 6 a.m., 9 a.m., 12 noon, 3 p.m. Each row is 3 hours.
steps.why: High to high is about 12 hours, so there are two high tides a day.

slips.msg: 6 hours is high tide to low tide. Count on to the next high tide.

items.prompt: The key words of the lesson. [[Choose the right meaning for each word.]]

steps.title: What is a tide?

options.text: The change in the depth of the sea during the day
A big wave in a storm

steps.line: Tide: the change in the depth of the sea during the day.
steps.hint: Think of the road to Holy Island: dry, then under the sea.

slips.msg: A wave comes and goes in seconds. A tide is a slow change in depth over hours.

steps.title: What is low tide?
steps.hint: Low means the water is down.

slips.msg: The deepest water is high tide. Low tide is the shallowest.

steps.title: What is tidal force?

options.text: The pull of the wind on the oceans
The pull of the Moon’s gravity on the oceans

steps.line: Tidal force: the pull of the Moon’s gravity on the oceans.
steps.hint: What is pulling the sea? Something big in the sky.
steps.why: The Moon’s gravity pulls the oceans into two bulges.

slips.msg: The Earth spins through the bulges, but the pull comes from the Moon’s gravity.

options.text: Facing the Moon and on the far side

options.text: No: it is at right angles to the Moon

steps.hint: No bulge means the water is shallow.

items.prompt: At a harbour the average depth is {{7.0 m}}. The tidal range is {{3.0 m}}. [[What is the maximum depth?]]

steps.title: When is the water deepest?
steps.line: The maximum depth is at high tide.
steps.hint: Maximum means the biggest depth.

slips.msg: Low tide is the shallowest water. The maximum is at high tide.

steps.title: How far above the average?
steps.hint: The range is shared: half above the average, half below.

slips.msg: The water does not go the whole range above the average. Half is above, half is below.

steps.title: Add it to the average
steps.hint: The maximum is above the average, so add.
steps.why: Half the range above the average: 7.0 + 1.5 = 8.5 m.

slips.msg: 10 m adds the whole range. Only half of it is above the average.
5.5 m is below the average: that is low tide. The maximum is 7.0 + 1.5.

steps.title: How long from high to low?
steps.hint: High to high is 12 hours. Low tide comes halfway.

slips.msg: 12 hours is high tide to the next high tide. Low tide comes halfway.

steps.hint: Count on 6 hours from 2 a.m.

steps.title: Choose the time
steps.hint: 2 a.m. + 6 hours.
steps.why: A quarter turn of the Earth takes 6 hours: from high tide to low tide.

slips.msg: 2 p.m. is 12 hours later: the next high tide.
One hour is too short. High to low takes about 6 hours.

steps.title: Same time, earlier or later?
steps.line: Tomorrow high tide is a little later.
steps.hint: The Moon moves on a little every day. The Earth must turn a little more.

slips.msg: The Moon moves on every day, so the Earth must turn a little more to face it again.

steps.title: How many minutes later?
steps.hint: 24 hours ÷ 29 days is about this many minutes.

steps.title: Choose the time
steps.hint: 9:00 a.m. + 50 minutes.

slips.msg: 9:00 a.m. is the same time. High tide comes about 50 minutes later each day.
8:10 a.m. is 50 minutes earlier. It comes later, not earlier.

steps.title: Which days have big ranges?

steps.hint: Two days have ranges over 5 m.

slips.msg: Day 1 has a big range too: 5.6 m. There are two big days.

steps.title: What is the Moon like then?
steps.hint: Read the Moon column for day 1 and day 15.
steps.why: The tides are biggest when the Sun, the Moon and the Earth are in a line: new moon and full moon.

slips.msg: At half moon the ranges are small (2.4 m and 2.2 m). They are at right angles then.
Day 1 is a new moon, and its range is big too. New moon and full moon.

items.prompt: At a river mouth the average depth is {{4.0 m}}. The tidal range is {{2.6 m}}. [[How deep is the water at low tide?]]

steps.title: How far below the average?
steps.hint: The range is shared: half above the average, half below.

steps.title: Take it away from the average
steps.hint: Low tide is below the average, so subtract.

slips.msg: 1.4 m takes away the whole range. Only half of it is below the average: 1.3 m.
5.3 m is above the average: that is high tide. Low tide is 4.0 − 1.3.
6.6 m adds the whole range. Low tide is below the average, by half the range.

steps.hint: High tide comes a little later every day.

steps.title: Count on past midnight
steps.hint: How many minutes from 11:30 to 12:00?

steps.title: Choose the time
steps.line: High tide tomorrow night: about @ (after midnight).
steps.hint: 30 minutes gets to midnight. Then 20 more.

slips.msg: 11:30 p.m. is the same time. High tide is about 50 minutes later each day.
10:40 p.m. is 50 minutes earlier. It comes later, not earlier.
12:50 a.m. adds 50 minutes to midnight. 30 of the 50 minutes get you to midnight.

steps.hint: Do the same for harbour B.

steps.title: Find the difference between the ranges

steps.hint: Subtract the smaller range from the bigger one.

7.6 m adds the two ranges. How much bigger means subtract.
